title: Everyday verbs 3
about: Verb + noun collocations with have, take and pay, such as have a break, take a risk and pay a compliment, where Ukrainian often uses a different verb.

parts.title: Tip
parts.note: Порада з книжки: у звичайних дієслів (break, fall, run, take) бувають сильні й несподівані сполучення. Помічай їх і записуй цілими фразами. З деякими іменниками природно звучать два дієслова: have a break = take a break. Британці частіше кажуть have, американці — take. А от make і do тут не підходять. «Приймати душ» — have / take a shower, а не accept a shower. У таблиці — сполучення з юніту та їхні природні замінники.

rows: Let's take a five-minute break and open the windows.
Take a look at this old photo of Grandma.
have a holiday · go on holiday
We usually go on holiday in September, when it's quieter.
The whole class went on a trip to the zoo.
I catch the 7.40 train every morning.
Why run the risk of missing the plane? Let's leave early.
Make use of the hotel pool. It's free for guests.
I always have a shower as soon as I get home from the gym.

items.pattern: have an accident · have a bad / small / car accident
items.meaning: get hurt or damage something in an unexpected event, like a crash or a fall
items.example: My uncle **had an accident** at work and hurt his back.
more: She **had a small accident** in the kitchen and cut her finger.
Our neighbour **had a bad accident** on his motorbike last year.
items.watchOut: «Потрапити в аварію» — have an accident, не make an accident. «Спричинити аварію» — cause an accident. Обережно: про маленьких дітей had an accident часто означає «обмочився».

items.pattern: have an argument / a row (with sb) (about sth)
items.meaning: disagree with someone angrily
items.example: My brother and I **had a row** about whose turn it was to wash up.
more: They **had an argument** about money and didn't speak for a week.
I don't want to **have an argument** with you in front of the children.
items.watchOut: Row у значенні «сварка» — розмовне британське слово, вимовляється /raʊ/, як now. Row /rəʊ/ — це «ряд». Посваритися з кимось — have an argument WITH sb ABOUT sth.

items.pattern: have a (short / coffee / lunch) break
items.meaning: stop working or doing something for a short time to rest
items.example: We've been driving for three hours. Let's **have a break** at the next services.
more: The children **have a break** at half past ten and eat their snacks.
I'm exhausted. Can we **have a quick break**?
items.watchOut: «Зробити перерву» — не make / do a break. Кажуть have a break або take a break, обидва правильні. Make a break for it — це «кинутися тікати».

items.pattern: have a conversation / a chat (with sb) (about sth)
items.meaning: talk with someone; a chat is short, friendly and informal
items.example: I **had a long chat** with my neighbour over the garden fence.
more: Can we **have a conversation** about the holiday plans tonight?
We **had a chat** over coffee and caught up on all the news.
items.watchOut: Не make a conversation. Make conversation (без a) — підтримувати ввічливу розмову з малознайомими людьми: It's hard to make conversation at parties.

items.pattern: have difficulty (in) doing sth · have difficulty with sth · have no / some difficulty
items.meaning: find something hard to do
items.example: My grandad **has difficulty** reading small print without his glasses.
more: We **had no difficulty** finding the hotel.
Lots of children **have difficulty** with spelling at first.
items.watchOut: Після difficulty — дієслово з -ing: have difficulty finding, а не to find. Зазвичай без a: have difficulty, не have a difficulty.

items.pattern: have a (strange / bad) dream (about sth) · have a nightmare · have nightmares
items.meaning: see pictures and events in your mind while you sleep; a nightmare is a frightening one
items.example: I **had a strange dream** about my old school last night.
more: Our son **had a nightmare** and came into our bed at three in the morning.
After that horror film I **had nightmares** for a week.
items.watchOut: «Бачити сон» — не see a dream. Кажуть have a dream або dream about sth: I had a dream about you / I dreamt about you.

items.pattern: have a(n) (amazing / strange / frightening) experience
items.meaning: something happens to you that affects how you feel
items.uk: пережити щось (цікаве, страшне), з тобою щось трапилося
items.example: We **had an amazing experience** swimming with dolphins in Greece.
more: I **had a strange experience** on the night bus last week.
She **had a terrible experience** at the dentist as a child and is still nervous.
items.watchOut: Experience буває злічуваним — «випадок, враження» (an amazing experience), і незлічуваним — «досвід» (work experience, без a). «Набути досвіду» — gain / get experience.

items.pattern: have a feeling (that) … · have the feeling (that) …
items.meaning: think that something is true or will happen, without being sure
items.example: I **have a feeling** we've forgotten something. Did you lock the back door?
more: She **had a feeling** that someone was following her.
I **had a feeling** you'd call today!
items.watchOut: «У мене таке відчуття» — I have a feeling (that)…, не I feel a feeling. У розмові кажуть і I've got a feeling…

items.pattern: have fun · have great fun · have a good / great / lovely time
items.meaning: enjoy yourself
items.example: The kids **had fun** at the water park all afternoon.
more: Bye! **Have a good time** in Paris!
We **had a lovely time** at my cousin's wedding.
items.watchOut: «Добре провести час» — have a good time, не spend a good time. Fun — незлічуване: have fun, без a. Make fun of sb — це «насміхатися з когось».

items.pattern: have a look (at sth) · have a quick look (round / in sth)
items.meaning: look at something, often quickly, to check it or find out about it
items.example: Could you **have a look at** my bike? The brakes are making a strange noise.
more: I'll **have a quick look** in the fridge and see what we need.
We **had a look** round the market before lunch.
items.watchOut: Take a look теж правильно (так частіше кажуть американці). Не make a look. Дивитися НА щось — have a look AT sth, не on.

items.pattern: have a (birthday / leaving / surprise) party
items.meaning: organise a party and invite people
items.example: We're **having a party** on Saturday to celebrate moving into our new flat.
more: They **had a big party** in the garden when their daughter finished school.
We **had a party** for Grandad's eightieth birthday.
items.watchOut: «Влаштувати вечірку» — не make a party. Кажуть have a party, а також give / throw a party.

items.pattern: have a problem / problems (with sth) · have problems doing sth
items.meaning: something is causing you trouble or is difficult for you
items.uk: мати проблеми (з чимось), щось не виходить
items.example: We **had problems** with the heating all winter.
more: Call me if you **have any problems** finding the house.
My car **has a problem** with the brakes, so I'm taking the bus today.
items.watchOut: Не make problems. «Створювати проблеми» — cause problems. Have problems DOING sth (з -ing): She had problems getting to sleep.

items.pattern: have a try / a go (at sth / at doing sth) · have a go on sth
items.meaning: try to do something, often for the first time
items.example: That climbing wall looks scary, but I'll **have a go**.
more: Can I **have a go** on your skateboard?
I've never made bread before, but I'll **have a try**.
items.watchOut: «Спробувати» — have a go / have a try, не make a try. Have a go — розмовне британське. Have a go AT sb — інше: «накинутися на когось з критикою».

items.pattern: take a holiday · take a week's holiday · take your holiday (in August)
items.meaning: have a period away from work or school, often travelling somewhere
items.example: We haven't **taken a holiday** for two years, so we're going to Portugal in June.
more: You look exhausted. Why don't you **take a holiday**?
I'm **taking a week's holiday** in October to visit my parents.
items.watchOut: Holiday у британській — і «відпустка», і «відпочинок у поїздці». Так само правильно have a holiday або go on holiday (без a). Американці кажуть vacation.

items.pattern: take a (day / boat) trip (to somewhere)
items.meaning: go on a short journey to a place and come back
items.example: On Sunday we **took a boat trip** round the bay.
more: Let's **take a day trip** to the seaside while the weather's nice.
My parents **took a trip** to Scotland for their anniversary.
items.watchOut: Trip — поїздка кудись і назад. «Подорож» як сама дорога — a journey; travel — подорожі взагалі, без a: не a nice travel. Також кажуть go on a trip.

items.pattern: take a / the train / bus / taxi (to somewhere)
items.meaning: travel somewhere by train, bus, etc.
items.example: If you miss the last train, you can **take a bus** from the station.
more: We **took the train** to Lviv and then a taxi to the hotel.
I usually **take the bus** to work, but today I walked.
items.watchOut: «Поїхати автобусом» — take / get / catch the bus або go by bus (без the). «Сісти в автобус» — get on the bus, не sit on the bus.

items.pattern: take a liking to sb / sth · take an instant liking to
items.meaning: start to like someone or something, often quickly
items.example: Our dog **took a liking to** the postman and now waits for him every morning.
more: My grandma **has taken a liking to** green tea.
The kids **took a liking to** their new teacher straight away.
items.watchOut: Прийменник — TO: take a liking to sb. І порядок інший, ніж в українській: не «він мені сподобався», а I took a liking to him.

items.pattern: take a risk · take risks · take the risk of doing sth
items.meaning: do something although something bad might happen
items.example: He **took a big risk** when he left his job to open a café.
more: My grandparents never **take risks** with money.
We were **taking a risk** going hiking without a map.
items.watchOut: «Ризикувати» — take a risk або просто risk sth. Також правильно run a risk / run the risk of. Не make a risk.

items.pattern: take an interest in sb / sth · take a great / real interest in
items.meaning: become interested in someone or something and pay attention to them
items.example: My son has **taken an interest in** cooking, so he makes dinner on Fridays.
more: The museum guide **took an interest in** our questions and gave us a private tour.
She's always **taken a real interest in** her neighbours.
items.watchOut: Прийменник — IN: interest in sth, не to / for (калька з «інтерес до»).

items.pattern: take a photo / photos / a picture (of sb / sth)
items.meaning: use a camera or phone to make a picture
items.example: We asked a waiter to **take a photo** of the whole family.
more: I **took loads of photos** of the sunset from the balcony.
You're not allowed to **take pictures** inside the museum.
items.watchOut: «Зробити фото» — take a photo, не make a photo і не do a photo. «Сфотографуватися» (коли фотографує хтось інший) — have your photo taken.

items.pattern: take a chance · take a chance on sb / sth
items.meaning: do something although you are not sure it will work out
items.example: There were no tickets left online, but we **took a chance** and went to the box office.
more: I **took a chance** and asked her out, and she said yes!
The shop doesn't usually give refunds, but I'll **take a chance** and ask.
items.watchOut: Take a chance — «ризикнути». Не плутай з have / get a chance (to do sth) — «мати нагоду»: I didn't get a chance to call you.

items.pattern: take a dislike to sb / sth · take an instant dislike to
items.meaning: start to dislike someone or something, often for no clear reason
items.uk: одразу відчути неприязнь, не сподобатися з першого погляду
items.example: My son **took a dislike to** his new football coach after the first training session.
more: I **took an instant dislike to** the man who pushed in front of me in the queue.
For some reason, my sister's cat **has taken a dislike to** me.
items.watchOut: Як і take a liking — прийменник TO: take a dislike to sb.

items.pattern: take advantage of sth / sb · take full advantage of
items.meaning: make good use of a chance or situation; (of a person) use someone unfairly
items.example: We **took advantage of** the sunny weather and painted the fence.
more: **Take advantage of** the January sales if you need a new coat.
He's so kind that people sometimes **take advantage of** him.
items.watchOut: «Скористатися» — take advantage OF, не use advantage і не make advantage. Про людину значення негативне: take advantage of sb — використовувати когось.

items.pattern: take action (to do sth / against sb) · take immediate / urgent action
items.meaning: do something to deal with a problem
items.example: The council finally **took action** and repaired the broken street lights.
more: If your neighbours are too noisy, you should **take action**.
When the river started rising, the village **took action** and built a wall of sandbags.
items.watchOut: «Вжити заходів, діяти» — take action (без a), не make / do action. А «прийняти рішення» — make a decision (британці кажуть і take a decision), не accept a decision: accept a decision означає «погодитися з чужим рішенням».

items.pattern: pay attention (to sb / sth) · pay close / no / any attention
items.meaning: watch, listen or think about something carefully
items.example: **Pay attention** to the road signs. The speed limit changes a lot here.
more: The kids weren't **paying attention** and missed their stop.
My dog never **pays any attention** when I call him.
items.watchOut: «Звертати увагу НА щось» — pay attention TO sth, не make attention і не attention on. «Привертати увагу» — attract / draw attention.

items.pattern: pay sb a compliment (on sth) · pay a compliment to sb
items.meaning: say something nice about someone or what they have done
items.example: A stranger on the bus **paid me a compliment** on my coat.
more: He's shy and finds it hard to **pay compliments**.
She **paid her mother-in-law a compliment** on her cooking.
items.watchOut: «Зробити комплімент» — pay sb a compliment (у розмові ще give sb a compliment), але не make a compliment і не say a compliment. Комплімент ЩОДО чогось — compliment ON sth.

items.pattern: pay your respects (to sb) · pay your last respects (to sb)
items.meaning: visit someone or go to a funeral to show respect; last respects are paid at a funeral
items.uk: віддати шану; віддати останню шану (на похороні)
items.example: Hundreds of fans came to **pay their last respects** to the singer.
more: The whole village went to the church to **pay their respects** to the old doctor.
When we arrived, we went to **pay our respects** to Grandad's oldest friend.
items.watchOut: «Віддати шану» — pay your respects, не give respects. Respects тут завжди в множині. Give my respects to … — інше, дуже формальне «передай мої вітання».

items.pattern: pay tribute to sb / sth [formal] · pay tribute to sb's work / courage
items.meaning: say in public how much you admire or thank someone
items.example: In her wedding speech, the bride **paid tribute to** her late grandmother.
more: The mayor **paid tribute to** the firefighters who saved the old library.
After the match, the captain **paid tribute to** the fans who had travelled all that way.
items.watchOut: Зазвичай без a: pay tribute to; з прикметником буває й a: pay a warm tribute to. Не give tribute. Це офіційний стиль: промови, новини.

warmup.uk: Він зробив мені комплімент щодо моєї сукні.
warmup.q: He ___ me a compliment on my dress.
warmup.explain: Зробити комплімент — pay sb a compliment (у розмові ще give). Make тут не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Ми зробили купу фотографій на весіллі.
warmup.q: We ___ loads of photos at the wedding.
warmup.explain: Фотографувати — take photos, не make і не do.

warmup.uk: Минулої ночі мені наснився жахливий сон про іспити.
warmup.q: I ___ a terrible nightmare about my exams last night.
warmup.explain: Сон англійською не «бачать»: have a dream / a nightmare.

warmup.uk: Ми чудово провели час на морі.
warmup.q: We ___ a great time at the seaside.
warmup.explain: Добре провести час — have a good time. Spend потребує конкретного часу: spend a day, spend two hours.
Влаштувати вечірку — have a party (ще give / throw a party), не make.

warmup.uk: Якщо ми не почнемо діяти зараз, буде пізно.
warmup.q: If we don't ___ action now, it'll be too late.

warmup.uk: Не звертай уваги на його слова.
warmup.q: Don't ___ any attention to what he says.
warmup.explain: Звертати увагу на щось — pay attention to sth.

warmup.uk: Скористаймося знижками й купімо новий холодильник.
warmup.q: Let's ___ advantage of the discounts and buy a new fridge.
warmup.explain: Скористатися — take advantage of. Use advantage і make advantage — кальки.

A.q: Let's ___ a short break and stretch our legs.
A.explain: Зробити перерву — have a break (або take a break), не make / do.

A.q: Before my driving test I ___ a horrible dream that I'd forgotten how to drive.
A.explain: Сон англійською «мають»: have a dream. See a dream — калька.

A.q: Thanks for the party. We ___ a great time!
A.explain: Добре провести час — have a good / great time, не spend.

B.q: Could you ___ a photo of me and my mum?
Our son has taken an interest ___ old cars.
B.explain: Цікавитися чимось — take an interest IN sth, не to / for.

B.q: We ___ advantage of the cheap tickets and went to Paris for the weekend.

C.q: My boss rarely ___ anyone a compliment.
C.explain: Зробити комплімент — pay sb a compliment.

C.q: You'll miss the instructions if you don't ___ attention.
C.explain: Бути уважним, звертати увагу — pay attention.

C.q: At the memorial service, her colleagues ___ tribute to her kindness.
C.explain: Віддати належне — pay tribute to sb / sth.

example.title: A week in the Carpathians
example.uk:
Минулого літа ми нарешті взяли відпустку й поїхали в Карпати. Другого дня ми поїхали автобусом до гірського озера і перепливли його на човні. Я зробив купу фотографій.

Посеред озера небо потемніло, і в мене було відчуття, що насувається гроза. На щастя, човняр уважно стежив за хмарами й вчасно повернув назад.

Того вечора ми довго балакали з господинею нашої садиби. Вона одразу вподобала наших дітей і показала їм, як пекти млинці. Моя донька теж спробувала і дуже пишалася собою. Ми всі чудово провели час, і ніхто не хотів їхати додому.
example.en:
Last summer we finally [[took a holiday|b1]] and went to the Carpathians. On the second day we [[took a bus|b3]] to a mountain lake and [[took a boat trip|b2]] across it. I [[took loads of photos|b7]].

Halfway across, the sky went dark, and I [[had a feeling|a8]] that a storm was coming. Luckily, the boatman [[paid attention|c1]] to the clouds and turned back early.
